title: Warroom comms decision tree and customer bridging
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight runbook for running the war-room communications flow in the first four hours of an incident and for bridging to customers when appropriate. Focus: clarity, short cadence, and a single source of truth for external and internal updates.

Scope:
- Applies to Sev1/Sev2 platform incidents that affect API availability, major degradation, or data loss risk.
- Not intended to replace full postmortem docs — this is the immediate comms protocol.

Key roles (quick primer):
- Bridge Lead (BL): owns the timeline and drafts the canonical update. Starts the conference bridge, assigns scribes.
- Tech Lead (TL): owns triage and status (root-cause direction).
- Customer Liaison (CL): coordinates external comms and legal/CS approvals when required.
- Scribe: writes timeline and captures action items and decisions.

Decision tree (do this within first 10 minutes):
1) Verify impact window and blast radius. Who/what is affected? API endpoints, regions, models, embeddings?
2) Severity mapping: if >10% of requests or key customers impacted OR service errors >5% sustained for >5min => treat as Sev1.
3) If Sev1 or extended degradation: start bridge and post initial status page entry (T+10).
4) If isolated to non-critical background job or single customer: open a scoped ticket and notify impacted customer(s) privately; no public status page update required.

Internal war-room checklist (pre-bridge / immediate actions, T+0–T+10):
- BL: create incident channel (Slack), pin canonical timeline doc, invite TL, CL, Scribe, infra on-call.
- Scribe: create one-line incident summary at top of doc: "INC-{{INCIDENT_ID}} — <one sentence summary>" and timestamp.
- TL: snapshot top metrics (error rate, latency P50/P95/P99, capacity). Paste quick graphs or links.
- BL: choose bridge medium (Zoom/holograph/meet) and post join link in channel.
- CL: identify customers that should be informed within first 30 minutes.

On-bridge cadence and templates (T+10, T+30, T+60, then hourly):
- T+10 (Initial public): BL drafts and posts status page: short, factual, scope, mitigation in progress.
- T+30 (Progress): update whether mitigation reduced impact, next actions, ETA if known.
- T+60 (Assessment): indicate progress; if no ETA, escalate to exec comms for customer outreach.
- Hourly thereafter until service restored or degraded condition stabilized.

Status page template (short/plain text, replace placeholders):
- Title: "Partial outage affecting {{AFFECTED_SERVICE}} in {{REGION}}"
- Body: "We are investigating an issue impacting {{AFFECTED_SERVICE}} which may cause increased error rates and latency for some requests. Our engineers are actively diagnosing. Impact: {{SHORT_BULLET_OF_IMPACT}}. Next update: within 30 minutes. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}."
- Post-mitigation note (when resolved): "Service is restored. Root cause analysis in progress; we will post a follow-up within 72 hours."

Customer-facing bridge template (email / ticket / CS template):
Subject: [Redwood] Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — {Short summary}
Body:
Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},

We’re reaching out to let you know we’re investigating an issue that may affect {{CUSTOMER_PRODUCT_OR_API}}. Impact: {{WHAT_CUSTOMER_SEES}}. Our engineers are actively working on a fix. We will follow up by {{T+30/T+60}} with an update. If you are seeing critical failures, reply and we’ll prioritize.

Status page: {{STATUS_PAGE_LINK}}
Incident lead: {{BRIDGE_LEAD_NAME}} (x:{{PHONE}})

Thanks,
Redwood SRE on-call

Slack announcement (short):
INCIDENT {{INCIDENT_ID}} — {{ONE_LINE_SUMMARY}} — Status: investigating. Join bridge: {{BRIDGE_LINK}}. Status page: {{STATUS_PAGE_LINK}}

Guidelines for customer outreach:
- Proactive outreach criteria: top 10% ARR customers impacted, regulated industries, or legally required SLAs.
- Tone: factual, avoid speculation, no mention of estimated root cause until validated.
- Approval: CL must rubber-stamp any message that includes compensation or SLA credit language.

Bridge playbook — roles checklist (on-bridge):
- BL: hourly cadence, decide on external/exec comms, approve status page copy.
- TL: present diagnostics and short tasks.
- Scribe: maintain timeline with exact timestamps for each change and customer messages.
- CL: prepare customer templates, contact CS managers for prioritized outreach.
- Infra/Ops: run recovery playbooks (restarts, traffic re-route, scale actions) and annotate action items in timeline.

Common quick recovery actions (checkboxes):
- Roll back recent deploys? (confirm commit IDs)
- Bump autoscale limits / add burst nodes? (region, fleet id)
- Clear cache/prefix KV? (prefix list)
- Close noisy circuit breakers / disable problematic feature toggles?

Escalation matrix (when to involve execs/legal):
- Exec comms: when incident impacts >20% of user requests for >1 hour or when major enterprise customers report revenue-impacting outages.
- Legal/compliance: when data integrity or potential data exposure is suspected.

Post-incident follow-up (first 72 hours):
- At 0–24h: send interim postmortem summary to internal stakeholders; include affected customers list and timeline.
- At 24–72h: publish a customer-facing summary and collect customer feedback through CS.
- At 72h–7d: finalize RCA, action items, owners, and estimated timelines for fixes.

Postmortem checklist (to close incident in tracker):
- Final timeline with exact timestamps (scribe).
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence (TL + infra).
- List of corrective actions (owners + ETA).
- Customer outreach log (who was notified, when, how).
- Postmortem review meeting scheduled and invite list.

Quick examples (realistic short samples):
- Initial status page: "Investigating increased 500 errors on inference endpoints (us-west-2). Some requests are timing out. Engineers investigating. Next update in 30 minutes."
- Customer note: "We’re investigating errors affecting model responses for your account. We know this can impact production traffic; we will follow up within 60 minutes with remediation steps or ETA."

Notes and hygiene:
- Keep every status update under 3 short bullets. Use the incident doc as canonical source; do not post conflicting messages in Slack or email.
- Mark messages with who approved them (BL/CL).
- Avoid technical jargon for customer-facing copy — focus on impact, mitigation, and next update.

Appendix: quick links (examples to include in linked_artifacts):
- Live metrics dashboard URL
- Deployment history link (recent commits)
- Incident ticket link (JIRA)

End of runbook.

Version notes: draft v0.3 — simplified decision tree and explicit customer bridge policy.
